Brazil Chemicals Industry Faces Credit Freeze Amid Plunging Demand

Brazil's chemicals industry is grappling with a severe credit freeze, as plummeting domestic demand and tightening global financing conditions have left major producers struggling to secure working capital. The crisis, which intensified over the past two weeks, has forced several companies to halt operations at key plants and delay investment plans.

Braskem SA, Latin America's largest petrochemical firm, confirmed it has been affected by the credit squeeze. "We are in close dialogue with our lenders and taking all necessary steps to preserve liquidity during this challenging period," a Braskem SA spokesperson said on Wednesday. The company did not disclose the scale of its affected operations but acknowledged that negotiations with suppliers and banks are ongoing.

Industry association Sindicato Nacional da Indústria Química (SINQ) reported that at least nine medium- and large-sized firms, including regional player Novapol, have missed scheduled repayments in recent days. “Liquidity has dried up almost overnight,” said SINQ president Fernanda Silva. "With banks reluctant to roll over short-term debts, many companies are on the brink of operational shutdowns."

According to SINQ, overall chemical output in Brazil fell by 23% in May compared to the same period last year, while spot prices for key products such as polyethylene and caustic soda have tumbled by more than 30% since April.

Analysts warn that unless credit conditions improve swiftly, the crisis could deepen. "The chemicals sector is uniquely exposed due to its capital intensity and reliance on uninterrupted credit flows," noted Paulo Mendes, an industry analyst at Rio Investimentos. "The coming weeks will be critical."
